name: Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Seagrass, mangroves and reef on the Yucatan coast, ruled by crocodiles and jaguars.

tip.title: Strip the seagrass
tip.text: Seagrass beds feed manatees, green turtles and urchins and shelter young lobsters. Remove Turtle grass and watch the grazers and the crocodile and jaguar above them feel it.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Turtle grass
nodes.desc: Seagrass that carpets shallow lagoons and the reef back-waters. Larval spiny lobsters settle in these beds, and manatees and green turtles graze them.

nodes.name: Red mangrove
nodes.desc: Salt-tolerant trees along the coast and lagoons. Their roots shelter young marine animals and their leaves are eaten by manatees.

nodes.name: Florida thatch palm
nodes.desc: A coastal palm that is one of the most recorded plants near the reserve. Its fruit is eaten by animals such as spider monkeys.

nodes.name: Gumbo-limbo
nodes.desc: A common tropical forest tree. GloBI records many birds, bats and a monkey eating its fruit.

nodes.name: Long-spined sea urchin
nodes.desc: A grazing urchin of reefs and seagrass beds. Spiny lobsters eat sea urchins.

nodes.name: Green turtle
nodes.desc: Adults mostly graze seagrasses and algae in shallow lagoons. Large sharks and, on land, jaguars can take them.

nodes.name: West Indian manatee
nodes.desc: A large grazer eating many aquatic plants, mainly seagrass, plus mangrove leaves at high tide. It has almost no natural predators.

nodes.name: Mullet
nodes.desc: Schooling coastal fish of lagoons and mangrove channels. Crocodiles and pelicans eat them.

nodes.name: Central American agouti
nodes.desc: A forest rodent that eats fruit and seeds and buries some of them, helping trees spread. Jaguars and boas prey on agoutis.

nodes.name: Geoffroy's spider monkey
nodes.desc: A fruit-eating canopy primate. GloBI records it eating gumbo-limbo and palm fruit.

nodes.name: Jamaican fruit bat
nodes.desc: A fruit-eating bat that carries seeds around the forest. Boas are recorded eating it.

nodes.name: Caribbean spiny lobster
nodes.desc: Nursery in seagrass and mangrove, adult on reefs. It eats molluscs, urchins and other bottom animals, and is eaten by groupers and sharks.

nodes.name: Brown pelican
nodes.desc: A plunge-diving seabird of the coast that eats fish such as mullet. Turkey vultures are recorded eating pelicans.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A scavenger that cleans up carcasses. GloBI records it eating manatee, pelican, gray fox and boa.

nodes.name: Gray fox
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid that eats fruit and small animals. GloBI records it eating gumbo-limbo fruit and boas eating it.

nodes.name: Boa constrictor
nodes.desc: A constricting snake. GloBI records it eating fruit bats, agoutis, black iguanas and gray foxes.

nodes.name: American crocodile
nodes.desc: An apex predator of mangrove lagoons. Adults eat fish, birds, mammals and turtles, and in Quintana Roo fish make up most identified prey.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The top land predator. It ambushes mammals such as agoutis and can also take turtles; Yucatan forests are fragmented by roads and development.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong tropical light drives growth of seagrass, mangroves and forest.

nodes.name: Tides and lagoons
nodes.desc: Tides flood the mangrove and seagrass shallows with salt water and move nutrients and larvae in and out.

nodes.name: Karst groundwater
nodes.desc: Rain sinks straight through the porous limestone and surfaces as cenotes and springs, supplying the freshwater that wetlands and mangroves depend on.

nodes.name: Thin limestone soil
nodes.desc: Shallow soil over limestone; litter decay by microbes recycles nutrients to the forest.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, mangrove litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
